epics.title: CRM MVP
epics.description: A minimum-viable CRM for a working real estate agent. Contacts, leads and deals, with the follow-up cadence driven by lead type rather than left to the agent's memory. No implementation has started; the source doc is a capability list, not a design.
epics.requirements: Contact records are created and edited. A contact carries a lead type (buyer, seller, renter, landlord, investor, referral) and a lead source (website, Zillow, referral, open house, sign call, social). Notes attach to a contact, a lead or a deal. Calls, emails and meetings are logged as touchpoints. Deals move through pipeline stages. Lead type decides which funnel a lead enters and which follow-up strategy applies, and follow-ups are scheduled automatically from lead type plus stage. Everything is searchable and filterable by lead type, stage, source, status and recent activity.
epics.acceptance_criteria: An agent can take a new lead from first contact to a closed deal without leaving the app and without setting a single reminder by hand. Overdue follow-ups are visible on one screen. A pipeline view exists per lead type. Recent activity across all leads and deals is on one page.
epics.qa_tests: Creating a contact with each of the six lead types puts it in the matching funnel with the matching follow-up schedule. Moving a deal between stages reschedules the next follow-up. A follow-up whose due date has passed appears in the overdue view and nowhere else. Filtering by source returns only that source. No design or schema exists yet, so these are acceptance tests to write against, not a suite to port.

features.title: Contacts and lead records
features.description: The record layer: a contact, its lead type, its source, and the notes and touchpoints hanging off it.
features.requirements: Create and edit a contact. Tag with one of six lead types. Record lead source from a fixed vocabulary. Attach free-text notes to a contact, lead or deal. Log a call, email, meeting or other touchpoint with a timestamp.
features.acceptance_criteria: A contact round-trips through create, edit and read with every field intact. A touchpoint log reads back in time order.
features.qa_tests: A contact created with each lead type and each source reads back with that value. A note attached to a deal is reachable from the deal and from the contact. Touchpoints come back newest first.

features.title: Pipeline and deals
features.description: Opportunities moving through stages, viewable as a pipeline per lead type.
features.requirements: Create a deal against a contact. Move it through pipeline stages. Render a pipeline view filtered by lead type.
features.acceptance_criteria: A deal's stage history is recoverable. The pipeline view for one lead type shows only that type's deals.
features.qa_tests: Advancing a deal two stages and reading it back reports the current stage and both transitions. A pipeline filtered to 'seller' excludes a buyer deal.

features.title: Follow-up automation
features.description: The part that makes it a CRM rather than a contact list: the next action is scheduled by the system, from lead type and stage.
features.requirements: Each lead type has a follow-up strategy. A lead's funnel is decided by its type. Scheduling a follow-up is automatic on lead creation and on every stage change. Manual follow-up tasks and reminders are also settable. Overdue follow-ups surface on their own view.
features.acceptance_criteria: No follow-up ever has to be created by hand for the normal path. An overdue item is impossible to miss.
features.qa_tests: Creating an investor lead schedules the investor cadence and not the buyer cadence. A stage change reschedules rather than duplicating. A follow-up dated yesterday appears in the overdue view; one dated tomorrow does not.

features.title: Search and filtering
features.description: Finding a record across contacts, leads and deals.
features.requirements: Free-text search across contacts, leads and deals. Filter by lead type, pipeline stage, source, status and recent activity. A recent-activity view spanning leads and deals.
features.acceptance_criteria: Any record the agent remembers a fragment of is findable in one search.
features.qa_tests: A search term matching a contact name, a note body and a deal title returns all three. Two filters combined narrow rather than widen.

epics.title: Unified logging standard — rollout
epics.description: The standard is built and merged; this is the rollout to the apps that do not have it yet. Documented at docs/system-configuration/unified-logging-standard.md. The procedure per app: copy core/hive_logging.py into it (copy, never share — per-repo ownership), swap logging.basicConfig for configure_logging, add install_fastapi_logging to the FastAPI app, then instrument the mutation points with log_event.
epics.requirements: Every app's process logs are one JSON stream. Every mutation emits a named event with actor attribution. No secret and no message body ever appears in a log. Non-Python apps keep the record shape and the event vocabulary and port the formatter, which is about fifty lines in any language with a JSON library.
epics.acceptance_criteria: Done means all three of those hold for the app in question, not that the module was copied in.
epics.qa_tests: Per app: the log stream parses as one JSON object per line. A mutation through the app's own API produces an event naming the actor. A request carrying a bearer token and a message body produces a log line containing neither.

epics.title: Mind install automation
epics.description: Standing up a mind on a remote host is a manual procedure today. The two written procedures — docs/system-configuration/remote-baremetal-windows-mind-install.md (the Zach pattern) and docs/system-configuration/hivemind-spoke-install-requirements.md (the Arnold reference build) — are complete and proven, but they are guides a human follows, not something add-mind or setup-mind can execute.
epics.requirements: Three parts of the bare-metal-on-a-different-host case become automated: broker registration, soul seed, and voice. The soul is never auto-generated — the personality flow is driven by the user.
epics.acceptance_criteria: add-mind or setup-mind can stand up a remote bare-metal mind end to end, with the operator answering personality and voice questions rather than following a document.
epics.qa_tests: A run against a fresh host produces a mind the hub can reach, with a soul the operator dictated and a voice that speaks. A run with no broker row inserted fails loudly naming the missing row, rather than throwing a hub-side 500 with nothing pointing at the cause.

features.title: Automate the remote bare-metal install
features.description: The three unautomated parts of the cross-host case.

features.acceptance_criteria: No step requires reading a document and typing commands by hand.
features.qa_tests: End-to-end run against a fresh host.

stories.title: Automate broker registration for a remote mind
stories.description: Insert the remote mind's row with a LAN-reachable gateway_url and verify cross-subnet reachability. Today this is a manual afterthought, and its absence throws a silent hub-side 500 with nothing in the message pointing at the missing row.
stories.requirements: The install inserts the row with a reachable gateway_url and verifies reachability across subnets before reporting success. A missing or unreachable row fails loudly and names itself.
stories.acceptance_criteria: A mind installed on another subnet is reachable from the hub immediately after install, and a failure says which part is missing.
stories.qa_tests: An install that cannot reach the new gateway_url refuses with a message naming the URL and the subnet, not a 500.

stories.title: Drive the soul seed through setup-personality
stories.description: An interactive personality and backstory flow the user drives, reusing setup-personality. The character is never auto-generated.
stories.requirements: The install calls setup-personality and seeds the resulting soul into the KG against the new mind's UUID.
stories.acceptance_criteria: The new mind answers as the character the operator described, not as a generated default.
stories.qa_tests: Judged by talking to the installed mind: it answers to its own name and its own backstory. A mind with no KG Mind node is the known failure mode — Hex answered as Ada — so the test is that the node exists keyed to the new UUID.

stories.title: Wire the new mind's voice during install

stories.requirements: The install asks which engine, collects a reference clip or a catalogued voice name, and writes voice and voice_engine for that mind alone.
stories.acceptance_criteria: The new mind speaks in the chosen voice and no other mind's mapping changes.
stories.qa_tests: After an install naming a clip, that mind speaks in it; another mind on the same host still speaks in its own. A clip name that is not on the voice server is refused rather than silently falling back.

epics.title: Ollama Skill Agent
epics.description: A skill-plus-agent pair that hands a task to an Ollama-backed Claude session and streams the result back. The source doc is a full draft of both files — skills/ollama-task/SKILL.md and agents/ollama-task.md — not a description of one. Note that the drafted environment points ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL straight at a bare Ollama daemon on 192.168.4.64:11434, which is no longer how Ollama is reached: Ollama now binds loopback and containers go through ollama-bridge-relay, and inference is reached through the inference proxy. The draft needs that corrected before it is installed.
epics.requirements: A user-invocable ollama-task skill packages a task, an optional model and optional allowed directories as JSON and invokes the ollama-task agent. The agent spawns a Claude session against the Ollama-backed provider with stream-json in and out, passes the task in, streams JSON events back, and stops on the result event. Output is a JSON event stream: status, progress, result.
epics.acceptance_criteria: A task handed to the skill comes back as a streamed JSON result from a model served by Ollama, not by Anthropic. The provider is reached through the inference proxy with a bearer key, not as a bare daemon.
epics.qa_tests: Invoking the skill with a trivial task returns a result event. The spawned session's model is the Ollama-served one, verifiable from the proxy's own log. A call with no bearer key is refused by the proxy with 401 rather than silently reaching a daemon.

stories.title: Correct the drafted Ollama environment before installing the skill
stories.description: The draft sets ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL to http://192.168.4.64:11434 — a bare Ollama daemon. Ollama now binds 127.0.0.1 with the Host check on, containers reach it through ollama-bridge-relay.service on the docker0 gateway, and inference goes through the inference proxy, which answers 401 without a bearer key.
stories.requirements: Point the drafted environment at the inference proxy and declare the key. Drop the bare-daemon address.
stories.acceptance_criteria: The drafted spawn environment matches how every other Ollama-backed mind reaches inference.
stories.qa_tests: The skill's spawned session reaches a model and the proxy logs the request. The old address is gone from the draft.

stories.title: Install the ollama-task skill and agent
stories.description: Write skills/ollama-task/SKILL.md and agents/ollama-task.md as drafted, with the environment corrected.
stories.requirements: Skill is user-invocable, takes task plus optional model and allowed directories, and hands a JSON payload to the agent. Agent spawns the session, streams JSON back and stops on the result event.
stories.acceptance_criteria: The skill appears in the skills listing and a run streams events back.
stories.qa_tests: A trivial task returns status, progress and result events in order. The agent stops on result rather than hanging.

epics.title: The graph fan-out still puts names in URLs
epics.description: Started the week of 2026-09-21. contextual_retrieval.py — every mind's copy — pulls every capitalised token out of the user's prompt and sends each one to lucent as its own GET /graph/query?entity_name=<token>. One request per candidate name, per turn, in the URL. Zeek's http.log records it verbatim, so does uvicorn's access log, and both land in Loki. Live rows in the sentinel store on 192.168.4.16 show the shape: three requests for Traceback, Error and ERROR off one prompt about a stack trace. When the prompt is about a person, what lands in the log is a person's name, one line per name, timestamped and attributable to whoever was typing.
epics.requirements: Candidate names stop appearing in URLs. Either /graph/query becomes a POST as /memory/retrieve did, or the fan-out becomes one batched request carrying all candidate names — batching being the bigger win, since the fan-out is up to a dozen round trips on a prompt with several capitalised words, on the hot path of every turn.
epics.acceptance_criteria: No name reaches Zeek's http.log, uvicorn's access log or Loki by way of a URL. The hot path is no slower, and preferably faster.
epics.qa_tests: A turn whose prompt contains several capitalised words produces no access-log line carrying any of them. The same turn produces one request rather than a dozen if batching is the chosen route.

features.title: Close the leak
features.description: The change itself. hive-mind#252 moved /memory/retrieve to a POST body because the question was in the URL; this is a different route sending a different thing — a single extracted token, not the prompt. Same family of leak, separate change. Folding it into #252 would have widened a signed-off scope mid-flight.
features.requirements: Decide between POST and batching, then implement across every mind's copy of contextual_retrieval.py.
features.acceptance_criteria: No candidate name in any URL, in any mind.

stories.title: Decide: POST the query, or batch the fan-out
stories.description: Two routes. POST mirrors what #252 did for /memory/retrieve. Batching is the bigger win because it also collapses up to a dozen round trips on the hot path of every turn.
stories.requirements: A decision with its reasoning, covering both the leak and the round-trip count.
stories.acceptance_criteria: A decision another session can implement from without reopening the question.
stories.qa_tests: Not code. The artifact is the decision.

stories.title: Implement the chosen shape across every mind's contextual_retrieval.py
stories.description: Every mind carries its own copy, so this lands once per mind rather than in one shared place.
stories.requirements: The new call shape in every copy. No mind left on the GET path.
stories.acceptance_criteria: A turn on any mind produces no name-bearing URL.
stories.qa_tests: Per mind: a prompt with several capitalised words produces access-log lines carrying none of them. A mind still on the old path fails this, which is the point.

stories.title: Check whether the hive-sentinel sensor gate already covers this
stories.description: The gate added in hive-sentinel@1151c7c drops hive-origin traffic to a hive service, so these rows stop becoming events. But the names are still written into Loki and Zeek's logs, which is the part that matters.
stories.requirements: Establish what the gate does and does not cover, so the remaining exposure is known rather than assumed closed.
stories.acceptance_criteria: A clear statement of what still reaches Loki after the gate.
stories.qa_tests: A fan-out request after the gate: confirm no event is raised, and confirm whether or not a Loki row still carries the name. Both answers matter.

stories.title: Decide whether anything already in Loki needs purging
stories.description: Names are already written. The question is whether Loki's own retention window handles it or whether a purge is warranted.
stories.requirements: Establish the retention window and decide.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Either a purge is done or the retention window is recorded as sufficient.
stories.qa_tests: Not code. If a purge happens, a query for a known leaked name returns nothing afterwards.

epics.title: Credential rotation — outstanding work
epics.description: The console itself is built and merged; what it does is documented at docs/system-configuration/credential-rotation-console.md. This epic carries only what is still owed: the bind-mount deploy, two rotations, the Planka-orphaned pipeline skills, a safety net, and one open question about where the console lives.
epics.requirements: The .env bind-mounts go live. The GitHub PAT and the comms bearer tokens rotate. The orphaned dev-pipeline skills are either retired or repointed. A rotation log and a staleness alert exist.
epics.acceptance_criteria: The Credentials tab reads real files rather than empty ones, both rotations are done, and a credential that has not rotated in its configured window raises an alert.
epics.qa_tests: The Credentials tab shows populated .env contents after the restart. gh auth status reports the new token. A credential with a backdated rotation timestamp triggers the alert.

features.title: Deploy the mounts
features.description: The .env bind-mounts are only live after hive-site restarts. Until then the Credentials tab reads empty .env files, because /env_nervous_system/.env and its siblings do not exist inside the running container yet.
features.requirements: docker compose up -d hive on this host. Not on the hot path of any live conversation, unlike hive-comms — restart whenever convenient.
features.acceptance_criteria: The mounted paths exist in the container and the tab reads them.
features.qa_tests: docker exec into hive-site and the mounted .env paths exist and are non-empty. The Credentials tab renders their contents.

stories.title: Restart hive-site to bring the .env bind-mounts live
stories.description: docker compose up -d hive on this host. Safe to do whenever — hive-site is not on the hot path of a live conversation.
stories.requirements: The container comes back with the mounts present.
stories.acceptance_criteria: /env_nervous_system/.env and its siblings exist inside the container.
stories.qa_tests: docker exec hive-site ls on each mounted path returns a non-empty file. The Credentials tab is no longer blank.

features.title: Rotations still owed
features.description: Two credentials due for rotation, one of them deferred by standing rule.
features.requirements: The GitHub PAT and the comms bearer tokens both rotate.
features.acceptance_criteria: Both old values are dead and everything that consumed them works on the new ones.

stories.title: Rotate the GitHub PAT
stories.description: gh auth status shows a classic token (gho_...) with scopes gist, read:org, repo and workflow, logged in as danielstewart77. Manual — there is no rotation API.
stories.requirements: Generate the replacement in the GitHub UI, then gh auth login and update wherever else it is consumed.
stories.acceptance_criteria: gh auth status reports the new token and every consumer still authenticates.
stories.qa_tests: gh auth status succeeds on the new token. A push and a PR creation both work. The old token is revoked and fails.

stories.title: Rotate COMMS_BEARER_TOKEN and COMMS_ADMIN_BEARER_TOKEN
stories.description: In hive-edge-mind-skippy/.env. Requires restarting skippy.service and hive-comms, which kills the live conversation. Deferred to Daniel's chosen moment, per the standing rule against Skippy-initiated hive-comms restarts.
stories.requirements: New values in .env, both services restarted at a moment Daniel picks.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Every surface still authenticates on the new tokens and the old ones are refused.
stories.qa_tests: After the restart, a Telegram turn completes and a terminal attach succeeds. A call carrying the old token is refused with 401 rather than silently accepted.

features.title: Dev-pipeline skills orphaned by the Planka teardown
features.description: /hivemind:planka, /create-story, /story-start, /story-close and /orchestrator all called tools/stateless/planka/planka.py, deleted along with Planka on 2026-07-30. The live marketplace plugin repo already stripped these to setup-only skills; the local cache is stale relative to it.
features.requirements: Daniel's decision: retire the dev-pipeline skills entirely, or pick a replacement work-item source before restoring them. Worth noting that the kanban board these backlog items now live on is a candidate replacement.
features.acceptance_criteria: The skills either do not exist or work against a live work-item source.
features.qa_tests: Invoking any of the five either reports it is retired or completes against the replacement source. None of them fails on a missing planka.py.

stories.title: Decide: retire the dev-pipeline skills or repoint them
stories.description: Five skills call a tool that no longer exists. The console's own kanban is now a candidate work-item source, which it was not when this was written.
stories.requirements: A decision, then either removal or a repoint.
stories.acceptance_criteria: No skill on the machine calls the deleted planka.py.
stories.qa_tests: Invoking each of the five produces either a clean retirement message or real work against the new source.

features.title: Safety net
features.description: Rotation is only trustworthy if it is recorded and if staleness is noticed.
features.requirements: A rotation log saying what rotated, when, and what triggered it. An alert when a credential has not rotated in N days, configured per credential — PATs and passwords rotate less often than session tokens.
features.acceptance_criteria: Every rotation leaves a record, and an overdue credential raises an alert without anyone looking.
features.qa_tests: A rotation writes a log row naming the credential, the time and the trigger. A credential backdated past its window raises an alert; one inside its window does not.

stories.title: Record every rotation in a log
stories.description: What rotated, when, and by what it was triggered.
stories.requirements: A durable log row per rotation carrying all three.
stories.acceptance_criteria: The history of a credential is reconstructable.
stories.qa_tests: Rotating a credential writes exactly one row naming it, the timestamp and the trigger. A failed rotation writes no success row.

stories.title: Alert on a credential that has not rotated in N days
stories.description: N is configured per credential, because PATs and passwords rotate less often than session tokens.
stories.requirements: A per-credential window and an alert when it is exceeded.
stories.acceptance_criteria: An overdue credential is surfaced without anyone checking.
stories.qa_tests: A credential whose last rotation is one day past its window alerts; one a day inside it does not. Driven by injected time, not by waiting.

features.acceptance_criteria: A decision, so the next credential surface is not built in both places.
features.qa_tests: Not code. The artifact is the decision.

stories.requirements: A decision covering edge-only secrets specifically, since those are what motivate a second surface.
stories.acceptance_criteria: One home chosen and written down.
